summary: OEIS term search (oeis.org/search?q=...) for the failure list 105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969 returns no sequence; 288,336,4545 return only A287116. The reduction is covered: t*x*y-x-y = n iff (tx-1)(ty-1) = tn+1 (FRONTIER §2.3 divisor identity), so the t-form adds nothing.

A005097 identity (odd primes -1)/2 = non-values of 2xy+x+y is classical (2(2xy+x+y)+1 = (2x+1)(2y+1)). The general t-form t*xy-x-y=n iff (tx-1)(ty-1)=tn+1 is the divisor form already in FRONTIER §2.3 (K1′, D_t^±).

summary: Engineering only: an exact split-hyperbola enumerator for ES after fixing one denominator is what the repo's existing solvers already do (verify.py, divisor form in FRONTIER §2.1); the item adds no new test.

The cited reference (arXiv:2302.02143) is about the Scholz conjecture for addition chains (l(2^n-1) <= l(n)+n-1, n=2^m*23+7), with no lower-bound technique that transfers to ES certificate search; the 'bounded-depth enumerator' is engineering, not a lemma.

Residue-class identity certificates with an independent checker exist: scripts/ec_cert.py verifies polynomial identities 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx), integrality on residue classes and positivity from the certificate data alone.

The first step (an explicit polynomial bound on the minimal ES denominator from constructions) is not specified: the cited Tao slides are about Egyptian-fraction counting, not minimal denominators; no construction is given in the item to bound.

The premise fails on the source: the arXiv:1406.6307 abstract says Salez proved a complete set of seven modular equations, i.e. a finite family, so 'first k filters up to k = 10^3' is not available. The verification is to 10^17 with a finite sieve.

arXiv:2509.00128 (Mihnea & Bogdan) is already in the repo's literature memos with the 10^18 verification and f(p) evaluation; the repo's own solution-count data (f(p) ~ U(p) statistics, DISCOVERIES.md / z52_lit_es_direct.md) covers the comparison.
